body:
Thanks, good questions.

**Stack:** the builder is a Claude Opus 5.5 agent (Claude Agent SDK) running Blender 5.0 headless on fal GPUs. Item references come from GPT Image 2.5, 3D from Meshy 7.1 / Tripo H3.1 (picked per item), normalised to real-world scale. The agent writes a layout plan from the reference (positions, real dimensions, what rests on what) and builds it with Python. Deterministic checks then fix contact (ray-cast grounding to 1 cm), clashes, and validation, and a separate critic model scores the set against the reference before it ships. All of it is now in the repo: `builder/`, `SKILL.md`, `pipeline/`. Shots are rendered by github.com/apekshik/anyshot.

**Placement:** today it's agent placement plus geometric checks, so it's plausible and close to the reference, not pixel-registered. The reference fixes what's there and roughly where, by design. I agree a perception stage would make it tighter. Rather than YOLO (closed-vocabulary, 2D boxes), I'm looking at open-vocabulary detection plus segmentation and metric depth to back-project each object into 3D as a placement prior, with a measured per-object placement error against the reference.

**Scenes:** the `.blend` files are large, so they're not in git. I'll publish a few complete builds as downloads, with the build log and critic rounds, so you can see exactly what comes out.

fal does have a media server service so you can just store the large blend files there? 

how is the agent deciding which image2mesh model to use? how does it normalize to real-world scale (since it seems each fal model seems to have its own concept of scale). 

have you compared original image to the 3D. 

why not use MoGe3 for placement with more accurate depth and sizing https://huggingface.co/Ruicheng/moge-3-vitl 

i think it would be helpful to publish benchmarks on results
